name: Namo
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Only subclassification notes (Dohler 2012, Donohue); no grammar or phonology located

sources.citation: Endangered Languages Project: Namo (lang/2152), via the Internet Archive 2024
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; gives alt names Mari, Na, Dorro and dialects 'Mari Village', 'Tais Village' (identity only).

sources.citation: OLAC listing for ISO mxw (language-archives.org, as of Dec 2024, via the Internet Archive)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists only Glottolog, Ethnologue, transnewguinea.org wordlist and Rueck 2006/2011; no phonology, OPD or grammar for Namo.

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas. 2021. The phonetics of Southern New Guinea languages: an overview. In Lindsey & Schokkin (eds), Phonetic fieldwork in Southern New Guinea (LD&C SP24), ch.1.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Regional generalisation only (p.7): SNG phonologies show 'no tone, no pitch accent or distinctive stress except for Urama'; Namo is mentioned only for retroflex segments (p.~9), not treated individually for prosody.

sources.citation: Kashima, Eri. 2020. Language In My Mouth: Linguistic Variation in the Nmbo Speech Community of Southern New Guinea. PhD thesis, ANU. hdl:1885/201927.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Identifies Nä [næ] and Len as Nambu languages of Tais village (p.48) and says 'Descriptions of Neme and Nä are still to be conducted' (p.49); stress statement is for sister language Nmbo only (penultimate tendency, p.109) — nothing on Namo/Nä stress.

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas. 2012. Even more diverse than we had thought: the multiplicity of Trans-Fly languages. In Evans & Klamer (eds), Melanesian languages on the edge of Asia (LD&C SP5), 109-149. hdl:10125/4562.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Namo or on stress (family survey; examples from Nen).

sources.citation: Rueck, Michael J. 2011. Social Network Analysis Applied to Language Planning in the Morehead District, Papua New Guinea. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2011-037. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing (sociolinguistic survey). Table 3 (p.67, from Boevé 2002a) lists Namo = villages Tais, Mari; mentions an unpublished SIL Alphabet Development Workshop report (Boevé 2002a, ms.).

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas, Wayan Arka, Matthew Carroll, Yun Jung Choi, Christian Döhler, Volker Gast, Eri Kashima, Emil Mittag, Bruno Olsson, Kyla Quinn, Dineke Schokkin, Philip Tama, Charlotte van Tongeren & Jeff Siegel. 2018. The languages of Southern New Guinea. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area, 641-774. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with a university library login (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Family survey with Yam/Nambu phonology notes (mentions Namo retroflexes); may carry a branch-level statement on stress that would be the best second-hand source if Gore 2023 stays closed.

sources.citation: Gore, Elliott. 2023. A phonological description of Nä and Len: Two undocumented Yam languages of Papua New Guinea. MA thesis, Australian National University. 104 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open link recorded by Glottolog or the catalog, not checked; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked; the linked copy was not accessible when a reader tried
sources.note: The only phonological description of Namo (as Nä, Tais village) in existence per Glottolog (listed by Glottolog as a phonology, Glottolog's most extensive description 'phonology or text collection'); a 104-page phonology thesis will almost certainly have a prosody/stress section. Glottolog holds a private copy; not in ANU Open Research — obtain from author/supervisor (ANU CHL, Evans group) or Glottolog editors.

sources.citation: Siegel, Jeff. 2023. A Grammar of Nama: A Papuan Language of Southern New Guinea (Pacific Linguistics 668). Berlin/Boston: De Gruyter Mouton. §2.4.3 'Stress', pp. 46-47.

sources.access_detail: online with a university library login
sources.note: Closest fully described Nambu sister language (Nama); its stress section would calibrate any branch-level inference for Namo but is NOT a Namo source.

sources.citation: Boevé, Alma. 2002a. Morehead Alphabet Development Workshop II report. Ukarumpa: SIL, ms. (cited in Rueck 2011:67; produced trial alphabets incl. Namo for Tais/Mari)

sources.note: Unpublished SIL workshop report with a Namo trial orthography; unlikely but possible brief phonology notes; only other primary material on Namo besides wordlists.
